authority_boundaries.awc: owns task identity, dependency revisions, claims, leases, and terminal commits
authority_boundaries.awr: owns policy evaluation, reservations, dispatch decisions, and bounded retries only
authority_boundaries.awq: owns quality acceptance and evidence policy; scheduler cannot approve
authority_boundaries.awg: owns guidance and user-decision escalation; scheduler cannot decide
authority_boundaries.agent_registry: supplied preflighted profiles are consumed without discovery or mutation
authority_boundaries.agent_sessions: dispatch claims are handed to the provider-neutral session boundary

policy.queue: bounded admission with tenant and project backpressure
policy.fairness: priority plus virtual-time aging, then tenant/project service and stable tie-breaks
policy.resources: global, per-agent, per-tenant, per-project, and concurrency reservations
policy.dependencies: DAG readiness only after every dependency succeeds; terminal dependency failure propagates
policy.cancellation: queued cancellation is immediate and running cancellation fences further work
policy.retry: retryable failures consume an explicit bounded retry budget with virtual-time backoff

invariants: no dispatch without accepted Coordinator revision and preflighted agent profile
no global, tenant, project, agent, or resource overcommitment
dependency DAG readiness cannot bypass a predecessor
aging gives every continuously eligible finite job bounded progress
virtual service accounting prevents a tenant or project from monopolizing ties
backpressure rejects admission before reservation or dispatch
cancellation has priority over continued work and releases reservations only after the fenced acknowledgement
retry attempts and retry budgets are monotonic and bounded
dispatch claims carry lease fence, Coordinator revision, profile digest, and session identity
stale or expired claims cannot complete, fail, heartbeat, or acknowledge cancellation
same operation and request digest replay identically; conflicting replay rejects
scheduler cannot approve quality, guidance, user decisions, tests, specifications, or terminal commits
hostile_qualification: tenant/project/agent quota exhaustion and resource fragmentation
expired, crossed, replayed, and cancellation-fenced leases
retry budget exhaustion and delayed virtual-time retry
many-tenant starvation and deterministic concurrent tie interleavings
